stories.title: Students Win James Dyson Award for Device That Screens Students for Concussions in Just 60 Seconds
stories.label: health
stories.summary: Three students at Harvard built a simple, low-cost headset that can screen young athletes for concussions in just a couple of minutes using eye-tracking. It's cheap enough that schools without medical staff on hand could actually use it on the sidelines. Their invention just won the prestigious James Dyson Award, which recognizes real, working solutions to everyday problems. This means faster, safer decisions when a kid takes a hard hit during a game. It's a small piece of tech that could protect a lot of young brains.
stories.why_good: A real, working invention that just won a major award, making concussion detection faster and more accessible for kids in sports.

stories.title: Chinese Scientists Develop New Oil Refining Method That Cuts Energy Use by 90%
stories.label: technology
stories.summary: Scientists in China have found a clever new way to refine crude oil without the usual repeated boiling process that guzzles huge amounts of energy. Instead, they separate the oil's molecules at room temperature, and it actually worked in the lab. This could cut the energy used in oil refining by a stunning 90 percent. Refining is one of the most energy-hungry industrial processes on Earth, so a breakthrough like this could mean a lot less pollution and wasted power down the line. It's a great example of scientists rethinking an old, wasteful process from the ground up.
stories.why_good: A real, lab-confirmed breakthrough that could dramatically cut energy waste and emissions from a major global industry.

stories.title: Team Sequesters Plastic and Makes New Products Before it Breaks Down in Environment
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: A family in San Carlos, California has built a business around recycling the toughest kind of plastic there is. Nick Schick and his parents work with thermoplastics, the hard-to-recycle polymers that usually just pile up in landfills or break into microplastics. Instead, they melt them down and turn them into brand-new products before that plastic ever has a chance to pollute the environment. It's a simple, hands-on solution that's already up and running, not just an idea on paper. Small operations like this one show a real path for keeping stubborn plastic waste out of nature for good.
stories.why_good: It's a real, operating recycling effort that is already diverting hard-to-recycle plastic from the environment, not a proposal or study.
